# Fix `worklog_dir_flag` worktree resolution for worktrees under `<main>/.worklog/worktrees`

> **Provenance:** transferred from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT` (Tableau-Card-Engine
> store) by producer decision, where it was `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`
> (TCE worktree `wl-CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY-retire-legacy-choice-fields-and-the-clar`,
> commit `4975f6ff`), observed while running
> `render_report.py CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` from that worktree. The CG item is
> deleted after transfer; the full intake brief lives here.

## Problem statement

`shared/status_lifecycle._detect_worklog_dir()` builds ancestor candidates as
`parent / ".worklog"` for **every** parent, so when the cwd sits inside
`<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` the ancestor `<main>/.worklog`
itself yields `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`; it also accepts any `.worklog`
directory **without** checking that it is initialised. Both defects make
`worklog_dir_flag()` hand `wl` a store root that is either non-existent
(no-op flag) or uninitialised (`wl` fails with
`"Worklog system is not initialized"`), so skill scripts that shell out to
`wl` break when run from an `implement.py` worktree.

## Users

- **AI agent running skill scripts from an implement worktree** — `/skill:report`,
  `/skill:audit`, `persist_audit.py`, and status/lifecycle helpers all resolve
  the store through `worklog_dir_flag()` / `resolve_worklog_flags()`.
  Story: *As an agent finishing work in a worktree, `render_report.py <id>`
  must read the main checkout's worklog so my report is populated and my
  status transition is written to the store the producer reads.*
- **Producer / operator** — needs a trustworthy store resolution so a run from
  a worktree cannot silently target a wrong or uninitialised store.
  Story: *As the producer, when an agent reports from a worktree, the item it
  reports on must be the item in the main checkout's store, with no manual
  `--worklog-dir` correction.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs the resolution rule pinned by tests.
  Story: *As a skill maintainer, I need a regression test for the
  `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/…` layout so a future refactor of the ancestor
  walk cannot reintroduce a nested `.worklog/.worklog` path.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves to the main checkout store.**
      With cwd = `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` and no `.worklog`
      in the worktree, `worklog_dir_flag()` returns
      `["--worklog-dir", "<main>/.worklog"]` (the initialised store), including
      when a stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — no double suffix.** An ancestor directory already named
      `.worklog` is never extended to `.worklog/.worklog`; the worklog
      directory that is itself an ancestor is the candidate.
- [ ] **AC3 — initialised candidates only.** A candidate `.worklog` that is not
      initialised (`_is_initialized_worklog()` false — e.g. a worktree's
      committed `config.yaml`-only copy) is never returned; resolution
      continues to the nearest initialised ancestor, and returns `[]` (no flag)
      rather than an uninitialised path when nothing initialised exists.
- [ ] **AC4 — unit tests cover the worktree layouts.** New hermetic tests
      (tmp_path fixtures, no real `git worktree`, no network) covering:
      (a) `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` with a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` present;
      (b) a **subdirectory** of a worktree whose committed `.worklog/` holds
      only `config.yaml` (the uninitialised-candidate case);
      (c) a plain nested project cwd (no `.worklog` between cwd and the project
      root) still resolving as today (no regression).
- [ ] **AC5 — existing precedence preserved, no weakening.** Precedence
      `explicit --worklog-dir` > prefix-to-sibling scan > cwd chain > no flag is
      unchanged, and the existing tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` pass without
      edits to their assertions.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The resolution rule (initialised-only, no
      `.worklog/.worklog` nesting, worktree-ancestor special case) is stated in
      the code docstrings of `_detect_worklog_dir()` / `worklog_dir_flag()` and
      in `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` (the section that says
      `StatusLifecycle` resolves the worklog dir automatically) and
      `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (the worklog-store resolution note).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Fix lands in this repository.** The defective code is
  `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` here; `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to
  `skill/`. Do **not** edit another project's `.pi/`, and do not create a
  vendored copy of the helper.
- **Shared seam.** `status_lifecycle` is imported by every skill; keep the
  change narrow (one candidate-selection helper reused by both
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`), with no behaviour change
  for cwds that already resolve correctly.
- **Fail closed, never guess.** Returning no `--worklog-dir` (so `wl` reports
  the real error) is preferred over returning a path that is not an initialised
  store.
- **Hermetic tests.** No real `git worktree`/network in the unit tests;
  `unittest.mock.patch` on `Path.cwd`-derived inputs or `tmp_path` layouts,
  matching the existing test module's style.
- **Gate order.** build → test → commit, never reversed; no ad-hoc `pytest` —
  run tests through the test skill (`/skill:test` / `run_tests.py`).

## Existing state (verified during intake)

- Source of truth: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (this repo).
- `_detect_worklog_dir()` (line ~258) order: `<cwd>/.worklog` →
  `<git toplevel>/.worklog` → `for parent in cwd.parents: parent/".worklog"`;
  the last two gates call `is_dir()` only, never `_is_initialized_worklog()`.
- `worklog_dir_flag()` (line ~391) has a **second, different** ancestor walk
  that *does* check `_is_initialized_worklog()`, then falls back to
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` — so the two walks disagree.
- Reproduced (Tableau-Card-Engine checkout, registered worktree, git toplevel =
  the worktree):
  ```
  cwd=/home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>   (historical reproduction in a sibling project)
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> /home/rgardler/projects/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '…/Tableau-Card-Engine/.worklog/.worklog']
  ```
  The stale `…/.worklog/.worklog/` exists and contains only a `worktrees/`
  subdirectory (no `initialized` marker, no `worklog.db`).
- Reproduced (this repository, registered worktree, run from a **subdirectory**
  so the `cwd/.worklog` branch is skipped):
  ```
  cwd=…/.worklog/worktrees/<wt>/skill
  _detect_worklog_dir() -> <that worktree>/.worklog      # config.yaml only — NOT initialised
  worklog_dir_flag()    -> ['--worklog-dir', '<worktree>/.worklog']
  ```
  i.e. a second manifestation of the same defect (uninitialised candidate),
  at the worktree **root** even though the initialised main store is a direct
  ancestor. Both are in scope via AC1–AC3.
- `_resolve_repo_root()` already handles the worktree case for the framework
  root (`skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py::TestFrameworkRootDerivation`)
  — the framework root is correct; only the *store* resolution is wrong.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` covers prefix scan,
  `resolve_worklog_dir`, `resolve_worklog_flags` precedence and `run_wl`
  injection, but has **no** ancestor-walk / worktree-layout test.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` re-uses `worklog_dir_flag()`, so it is fixed
  transitively. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` resolves its own target
  project root and is unaffected.
- Adjacent same-class defect, **filed separately** by producer decision as
  `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` (see *Related work*):
  `skill/shared/code_freeze.py::_detect_worklog_dir()` (line
  ~48) duplicates the ancestor walk with the same `parent/".worklog"`
  construction and no initialisation check, so `code_freeze_marker_path()`
  would read `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json` from a worktree.

## Desired change

1. Introduce one candidate-selection helper used by both
   `_detect_worklog_dir()` and `worklog_dir_flag()`:
   - for each ancestor, if the ancestor **is** a worklog directory
     (`name == ".worklog"`), the candidate is that ancestor itself; otherwise
     the candidate is `ancestor / ".worklog"`;
   - only accept a candidate when `_is_initialized_worklog(candidate)` is true
     (in the `_detect_worklog_dir` gate; `worklog_dir_flag` keeps its existing
     "no flag" contract when nothing initialised is found).
2. Delete the duplicated walk in `worklog_dir_flag()` in favour of the shared
   helper (no second, divergent rule).
3. Tests per AC4, in the existing
   `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` module style.
4. Doc updates per AC6.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_detect_worklog_dir()` (~line 258)
  gains the `.worklog`-named-ancestor rule and the `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  gate; `worklog_dir_flag()` (~line 391) re-uses the same helper instead of its
  own walk; docstrings per AC6.
- `skill/shared/tests/test_shared_worklog_resolution.py` — new
  `TestWorklogDirAncestorWalk` class with the AC4 cases.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — the "`StatusLifecycle` resolves the same
  directory automatically" paragraph (~lines 84–88) gains the initialised-only /
  no-nesting rule.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` — worklog-store resolution note
  (~lines 360–364).

## Related work

- `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` (open, intake_complete) — *implement.py finish reports
  status changes that the main worklog store does not show*. Same seam, wider
  scope (finish must pass an explicit store). Its "Existing state" note claims
  `worklog_dir_flag` "does resolve the main checkout store from a worktree";
  the evidence above shows that holds only when no stale
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` exists — this item carries the counter-example.
  Partial overlap only, so **not** a duplicate.
- `SA-0MW0JI376007RON7` — `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's
  non-initialised `.worklog` (the same walk duplicated in `code_freeze.py`).
  Filed separately by producer decision (Appendix Q2) and **blocked by** this
  item, so the shared rule lands first.
- `CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — original discovery work item.
- `CG-0MUC5GVCJ0062BN7` (Tableau-Card-Engine, completed) — earlier
  worktree-resolution defect (`.pi/test-config.json` unseen from a worktree):
  same failure family, different file.
- `SA-0MSG57UNY009DE51`, `SA-0MSGH55OJ003WKYZ`, `SA-0MTOMCML900254CI`
  (completed) — the prefix-to-sibling seam and cwd-independence lineage this
  item extends.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: resolver regression elsewhere.** Other skills rely on
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` returning a non-initialised directory in exotic
  layouts. Mitigation: AC5 requires the existing suite to pass unchanged; the
  change only *narrows* accepted candidates, and `worklog_dir_flag()` keeps its
  "no flag" fallback so `wl` still reports its own error.
- **Risk: `.worklog`-named ancestor inside a normal project** (e.g. a directory
  literally called `.worklog` used for something else). Mitigation: the
  `.worklog`-named ancestor is only accepted when `_is_initialized_worklog()`
  is true.
- **Risk: styling split between the two walks** if only one is fixed.
  Mitigation: single shared helper (Desired change 1–2).
- **Scope-creep risk: fixing `code_freeze.py` in the same change.** Excluded by
  producer decision (Appendix Q2) — it is filed separately.
- **Assumption:** the "stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog`" directory is a local
  artefact (from an old run) and is not committed anywhere; the fix must not
  depend on its removal, because the nesting rule is wrong regardless.
- **Assumption:** unit tests can express the layout with `tmp_path` +
  `mock.patch` rather than creating real git worktrees (the existing module
  already models the framework-root worktree layout this way).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Where should the fix and its record land?** The defective code lives
  in SorraAgents (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`); the TCE checkout has no
  `skill/` tree, so a TCE `implement.py` worktree could not carry the change
  (the TCE-side `implement.py finish` fails closed on out-of-worktree edits).
  Options were: (a) transfer the item to the SA store; (b) create an SA item
  carrying code + tests, keep the CG item as a linked discovery record;
  (c) commit to SorraAgents `dev` from outside a worktree (breaks
  worktree-isolation). Agent recommendation: (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"SA create there then delete this item"* — create the
  SA item with the full brief (this item) **and delete** the CG item, i.e. a
  transfer rather than a linked pair. Source: operator reply in the intake
  session `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q2 — Fold in the adjacent `code_freeze.py` defect?** Options: (a) fix both
  in this change via one shared helper; (b) keep this item narrow and file the
  `code_freeze` fix as a separate `discovered-from` item. Agent recommendation:
  (b).
  **Answer (producer):** *"file separately"* — the `code_freeze.py`
  `_detect_worklog_dir()` duplicate-walk fix is filed as its own item; this item
  stays narrow. Source: operator reply in the intake session
  `herdr-1793666897-1472625-2858`.
- **Q3 — Duplicate-work check (agent-resolved).** Searched both stores
  (`worklog_dir_flag`, `worktree resolution`, `nested worklog dir`) —
  `SA-0MVK2G09X00239YL` is the only overlapping item and its ACs do not cover
  the nesting/initialisation defects, so no duplicate close or rewrite was
  applied; it is cross-referenced in *Related work*. Answer: **no full
  duplicate; partial overlap cross-linked.**

# `code_freeze.py` resolves a worktree's non-initialised `.worklog` (and can build `.worklog/.worklog`)

> **Provenance:** `discovered-from:SA-0MW0JHMJE006GWQB` (which was transferred
> from `CG-0MVZKL4WB000JPZT`, itself `discovered-from:CG-0MVZFVZK1003F8HY`).
> Filed separately by producer decision so the parent fix stays narrow.

## Problem statement

`skill/shared/code_freeze.py` carries its **own** copy of
`_detect_worklog_dir()`. It builds ancestor candidates as `parent / ".worklog"`
for every parent and accepts any `.worklog` directory without checking that it
is initialised. Consequences:

- from a linked worktree root whose committed `.worklog/` holds only
  `config.yaml`, `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
  `<worktree>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` — a marker file that can never exist,
  so the fail-closed freeze gate silently sees "no freeze";
- from `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>` (no committed `.worklog`), a
  stale `<main>/.worklog/.worklog` directory would be selected, giving
  `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

The correct marker in both cases is `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.

## Users

- **AI agent running `/skill:implement` from a worktree** — the implement
  workflow consults the code-freeze marker; reading the wrong path makes the
  freeze gate miss an active freeze.
  Story: *As an implementing agent in a worktree, an active code freeze must be
  detected, so I stop instead of landing a commit that the freeze forbids.*
- **Producer/operator** — an activated freeze must be effective immediately for
  every checkout.
  Story: *As the producer, when I activate a freeze, agents working in
  worktrees must observe it without extra `--worklog-dir` instructions.*
- **Skill maintainer** — needs one resolution rule, not two divergent copies.
  Story: *As a maintainer, code-freeze marker resolution must not silently drift
  from `status_lifecycle`'s worklog-dir rule.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — worktree root resolves the main marker.** With cwd at a linked
      worktree root that has a committed, **uninitialised** `.worklog/`
      (`config.yaml` only), `code_freeze_marker_path()` returns
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json`.
- [ ] **AC2 — no `.worklog/.worklog` nesting.** With cwd inside
      `<main>/.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`, the marker path is
      `<main>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` even when a stale
      `<main>/.worklog/.worklog/` directory exists.
- [ ] **AC3 — explicit `project_root` unchanged.** `code_freeze_marker_path(<root>)`
      still returns `<root>/.worklog/code-freeze.json` and is unaffected by the
      cwd-based rule.
- [ ] **AC4 — one rule, not two.** `code_freeze._detect_worklog_dir()` either
      re-uses the shared resolution helper from `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
      (preferred — no duplicated walk) or mirrors it exactly, with a comment
      naming the shared rule as authoritative.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit tests.** Hermetic `tmp_path` tests in
      `skill/shared/tests/test_code_freeze.py` for AC1–AC3 (no real
      `git worktree`, no network), alongside the existing marker tests.
- [ ] **AC6 — documentation.** The `code_freeze.py` docstrings state the
      initialised-only / no-nesting rule; if resolution is shared, note it in
      `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` next to the `StatusLifecycle` note.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Goal

Investigate, and then reduce, large tool-call results before they enter conversation history, so that a single oversized tool result does not inflate every subsequent model turn. Prefer the cheapest effective mechanism; a small-model compaction call is one candidate among several.

## Evidence (from the proxy incident 2026-11-03, LLM repo)

- A single tool-role message of 51,945 bytes (a full SKILL.md pasted into history by the audit skill) entered the conversation at 08:41:54. The conversation grew from 22 KB to 120 KB of content over 7 turns, and the prompt went 6,564 to 33,570 tokens.
- Every subsequent turn re-prefilled the growing tail on a local model measuring 143-303 tok/s prefill, producing 53 s and 72 s time-to-first-byte.
- The proxy priced that 51,945-byte append at 173 new tokens against a measured 12,936 (deficit_ratio 0.659), so the cost was invisible to admission control as well as to the agent.
- Session recordings and session jsonl files are available for measurement: ~/.llm-proxy/session-recordings/ and ~/.pi/agent/sessions/.

## Candidate approaches, cheapest first

1. Measure first: rank tool results by bytes/tokens across recorded sessions to identify which tools dominate (skill-body pastes, wl show --json dumps, file reads). Deterministic script, no model call.
2. Truncate with re-read: a Pi extension intercepts a tool result above a threshold, keeps head and tail plus an explicit "truncated N bytes, re-read with offset/limit" marker, and preserves the raw output on disk.
3. Reference instead of inline: content-address large or repeated payloads (skill bodies, already-read files) and substitute a short handle plus preview when the content is already in the prompt.
4. Small-model compaction at the boundary: the extension detects an oversized tool result and asks a small/fast model to compact only what the current request needs, prefixing the tool output with a purpose-built instruction. Must reuse the existing summariser slot (Qwen2.5-7B preset, parallel=1, as pinned by the proxy compaction_summarizer) so it does not contend with the main model, and must only escalate here when approaches 2 and 3 are insufficient, since it is a model call on the critical path.
5. Structured projections at the tool level: JSON field selection, summary-by-default with details on demand, and flags that keep payloads small at source.

## Constraints

- Compaction must be cheaper than the prefill it avoids. Measured saving: avoiding 13k prefill tokens saves roughly 45-90 s at observed rates, so a ~2 s small-model call is a clear win; the strategy must be justified against that budget.
- It must not lose information the agent later needs, and any lossy step must be recoverable (raw payload retained and re-readable).
- It runs on the same GPU as the workload it protects, so it competes for capacity -- another reason to prefer non-model approaches first.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A measurement report exists ranking tool-result payload size by tool and session, produced by a committed deterministic script (no model calls), with the top offenders named.
- AC2: Each of the five candidate approaches is assessed for (a) bytes/tokens saved, (b) added latency and GPU contention, (c) information-loss risk and recoverability, with a recorded recommendation.
- AC3: At least one non-model mechanism (truncate-with-re-read or reference-instead-of-inline) is prototyped as a Pi extension and validated against a real oversized tool result, with the before/after prompt-token counts recorded.
- AC4: If a small-model compaction path is implemented, it reuses the existing summariser slot, is benchmarked against the prefill cost it avoids, and includes a documented fallback when the summariser is unavailable.
- AC5: Documentation states the extension's threshold, behaviour and how an agent recovers truncated content, and the result is recorded against the originating LLM-repo prefill-pricing item.
data.title: Reduce large tool-call results before they enter conversation history

# Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` in SorraAgents

## Why

This project's worklog database is behind the installed `wl` version. Every `wl` invocation prints:

```
Worklog: database at /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/.worklog/worklog.db has schemaVersion=8 but the application expects schemaVersion=9. Required columns were repaired automatically. see 'wl doctor upgrade' to list and apply pending migrations
```

Required columns are being patched on every invocation instead of migrated, and the git hooks are stale. Discovered during the 2026-11-04 downtime-dispatcher RCA (the same finding exists across the other worklog roots).

## Pending work (from `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`)

### Schema migrations (0)

_None — only hooks below are pending._

### Outdated git hooks

- pre-push, post-checkout, post-merge, post-rewrite, worklog-post-pull

## Goal

As a maintainer, I want this project's worklog schema and git hooks fully up to date, so that `wl` stops auto-patching columns on every call and so every worklog hook behaves like the current template.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` afterwards reports `pending: []` and no hook whose `status` is not `up-to-date`.
2. `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` was executed against this project's database and applied the migrations listed above.
3. A plain `wl list --json` invocation no longer prints the `schemaVersion=8 … expects schemaVersion=9` warning.
4. **Data-safety check.** The count of items with `needsProducerReview == true` is identical before and after:
   `wl list --json | jq '[.workItems[] | select(.needsProducerReview == true)] | length'`
   Record both numbers on this item.
5. `wl doctor` reports no new findings attributable to this upgrade (any residual finding is recorded on a follow-up item, not ignored).
6. The before/after `--dry-run --json` output is recorded in a comment on this item.

## Plan

1. Capture the baseline: `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` plus the `needsProducerReview` count → comment on this item.
2. Run `wl doctor upgrade --confirm`.
3. Re-run `--dry-run` (expect nothing pending) and re-check the `needsProducerReview` count (must be unchanged).
4. If the upgrade touched tracked files (`.githooks/`, hook templates), commit them following build → test → commit order.

## Risks & notes

- `--confirm` applies migrations **non-interactively, including UNSAFE ones**. Review the `[UNSAFE]` entries above before running. The database is the runtime source of truth (SQLite); never edit `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` and never run `wl import` (destructive).
- If the `needsProducerReview` count changes, STOP, restore, and raise a `bug` against ContextHub's `wl` migration set instead of continuing — the drop/re-add cycle is the suspected cause of the permanent schema-8 oscillation.

## Provenance

Created from the 2026-11-04 overnight zero-dispatch RCA. Pi session `herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004`, log `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-ContextHub--/2026-11-04T07-55-10-163Z_herdr-1793778909-1527089-27004.jsonl`.

## Goal

Decide and implement how non-interactive (herdr-downtime-dispatched) audits avoid the in-main-slot pending-screens trap: a dispatched audit has no interactive invoking session to perform the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens, so by construction every dispatched parent audit lands in the unserviced state.

Discovered-from: SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (audit comment 2026-10-29, "Adjacent scope note 1"). Distinct from the D1/D2 resume defects: even with a working resume cycle, nobody services a dispatched audit's screens.

## Proposal (needs producer decision — not yet approved)

Have the dispatcher pass `--no-child-in-main-slot` for downtime-dispatched audits, or have `cmd_issue` detect a dispatched/non-interactive context and resolve `child_in_main_slot=False`, so child screens run in isolated `pi` subprocesses with the runner's own parsing/retry instead of being emitted for a session that will never run them.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The chosen mechanism is recorded on this item with the rationale (dispatcher-side flag vs. runner-side context detection) and the trade-off accepted (separate-process child audits cost one `pi` subprocess per child but need no interactive session).
- AC2: Dispatched audits no longer emit `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` screens that nobody services: a dispatched run either completes its child screens itself or reports a documented, actionable state.
- AC3: An interactive audit launched from an agent session keeps in-main-slot mode by default — no behaviour change for the interactive path.
- AC4: Regression coverage proves the resolution precedence for the new mechanism (explicit flag > env `AUDIT_CHILD_IN_MAIN_SLOT` > dispatch detection > default `true`), with `wl`/`pi` mocked (no real subprocess).

## Minimal implementation

- Preferred (dispatcher-side, smallest blast radius): pass `--no-child-in-main-slot` from the downtime dispatch command; add a test on the dispatch command construction.
- Alternative (runner-side): resolve the mode from a dispatch marker/env in `_resolve_child_in_main_slot` and log the resolution source.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_resolve_child_in_main_slot`, `cmd_issue` child-mode resolution
- dispatcher/downtime-worker command construction (herdr package) — locate before editing
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_child_in_main_slot.py` — `TestChildInMainSlotGateResolution`

## Dependencies

- Related to SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S (its resume fixes are a prerequisite for any in-main-slot dispatch to be recoverable, but this item is not blocked by it).

## Deliverables

- Producer decision recorded + implementation + regression test.

# `scripts/install_pi.sh` wires git hooks but never refreshes the globally resolved `wl`, so a stale `dist` can silently revert the canonical hook template

discovered-from:CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU (Tableau-Card-Engine — "Restore pre-push test-cache mirroring in the canonical wl hook template", AC2 tail clause: recorded as a follow-up, not fixed there)

## Problem statement

`scripts/install_pi.sh` installs and *wires* the project's git hooks
(`.githooks/*` copies + `core.hooksPath`), but it never refreshes the `wl` binary
those hooks depend on. On this framework, `wl` is not installed from a registry
— it is **npm-linked to the `ContextHub` checkout**, and `ContextHub/dist` is
gitignored. So the template that `wl init` / `wl doctor upgrade` emits is
whatever was last built into a *local, uncommitted* `dist`, which can predate (or
diverging from) the committed hook. The next `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` then
silently rewrites a consuming repository's `.githooks/pre-push` from that stale
template and deletes capabilities the repo legitimately carries.

The concrete incident class: `mirror_suite_cache` (the dev-push gate's
test-cache mirroring, `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` / ContextHub `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP`)
existed only in a stale `ContextHub/dist` build for a while. A rebuild of the
linked `wl` from a `dev` that lacked the template change, followed by
`wl doctor upgrade --confirm`, removes the capability from every consuming
repo, with exit 0 and no warning — the invariant "a worktree-originated `dev`
push leaves a green cached full-suite entry the main checkout can read" then
breaks silently.

## Verified facts (checked 2026-11-04 on this host)

1. **`wl` is npm-linked, not registry-installed.**
   - `npm ls -g --depth=0` → `worklog@1.0.27 -> ./../../../home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`
   - `/usr/local/bin/wl` → `../lib/node_modules/worklog/dist/cli.js`, which
     `readlink -f` resolves to `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/dist/cli.js`.
   - The package version stays `1.0.27` across template changes, so the version
     number alone cannot tell you whether the *template* is current.
2. **The template lives only in the built `dist`.** `ContextHub/.gitignore`
   line 86 ignores `dist`; `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` is compiled from
   `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` into
   `ContextHub/dist/doctor/hook-upgrade.js`, so the `wl` a machine runs is
   whatever branch/dirty state was last built there.
3. **The installer wires hooks but never touches `wl`.** The hook block is
   `scripts/install_pi.sh:317-412` (comment header at :317): step 1 copies
   `$SRC_DIR/.githooks/pre-push` (v3) or `pre-push.v2` into the project's
   `.githooks/` only when absent (:347-361), step 2 sets
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks` (:363-370), then it verifies the global
   context-audit skill (:373-380), per-project thresholds (:383-388) and the git
   identity (:390-408). There is **no** `npm run build`, `npm link`, `npm i -g`
   or version check anywhere in the installer.
4. **The destructive step is `wl doctor upgrade`, not the installer.**
   `ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts:98` emits the upgrade set and
   `upgradeHooks()` (`ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts:603-643`) writes
   every `outdated` hook with `fs.writeFileSync(hookPath,
   h.committedContent, { mode: 0o755 })` — a **whole-file overwrite** of the
   repo's committed hook with the template baked into the running `wl`, i.e. the
   stale `dist`. The result is reported as success ("Upgraded from
   .githooks/").
5. **Why it matters (consuming repos).** Every repository in the framework uses
   `core.hooksPath = .githooks`, so the hook file *is* the gate. After a stale
   rebuild + upgrade, `.githooks/pre-push` no longer mirrors the gate run's
   cache entries into the main checkout's `.worklog/cache`, and
   `run_tests.py --summary --suite all --json` reports `missing` at the just-
   pushed commit (and audit F3 loses its cached green evidence).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Fail loudly on template skew.** The installer (and/or the hook-wiring
  step it owns) fails loudly — non-zero exit or an explicit, actionable
  `WARNING` naming both sides — when the template baked into the resolved `wl`
  predates/differs from the hook the repository commits, instead of leaving the
  operator with a `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` that deletes the divergence.
  *Verification:* a new test case drives the installer with a sandboxed `HOME`
  and a stub `wl` whose template lacks a marker present in the repo's committed
  hook, and asserts the refusal/warning text; the up-to-date case stays silent.
- **AC2 — Regression test in the existing installer suite.**
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` gains the skew cases next to the
  existing hook-wiring cases, with a sandboxed `HOME` (no live `~/.pi`, no live
  npm global root) so the test is hermetic and CI-safe.
  *Verification:* the new cases fail against today's installer and pass after
  the change.
- **AC3 — Documented.** The installer's own documentation and the hook-wiring
  docs state the dependency on the resolved `wl` and how to refresh it
  (`docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` global-install section,
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` hook-wiring section, `README.md` install entry
  as needed).
  *Verification:* each touched page names the `wl`-refresh step (or the new
  guard) and the failure it prevents.

## Candidate remedies (pros / cons)

**(a) Detect a `ContextHub` checkout and rebuild (or reinstall) the global `wl`
during install.** Resolve the global `worklog` link target; if it is inside a
git checkout, run `npm run build` there (or `npm link`/`npm i -g` when the link
is absent).
- *Pros:* removes the root cause on developer machines; one command still sets
  everything up; no new convention for consuming repos.
- *Cons:* gives a global installer a cross-repo build responsibility (slow,
  needs the link target's dependencies and a working toolchain); it builds
  whatever branch/dirty state that checkout happens to be on, so it can install
  the *wrong* template just as silently; surprising side effect for anyone who
  did not expect the installer to mutate `../ContextHub`.

**(b) Pin an explicit `worklog` version and refuse to run against an unexpected
one.** Commit the expected version (e.g. in the project's installer config or
`package.json`) and have the installer compare it with `wl --version`.
- *Pros:* deterministic and fail-loud; makes the dependency visible in every
  repo; cheap to implement; no cross-repo mutation.
- *Cons:* version numbers do not prove template equality — two builds of
  `1.0.27` can carry different templates, which is exactly the observed hazard;
  a mismatch blocks the operator until they rebuild by hand; needs a per-repo
  convention to keep the pin current.

**(c) Fail loudly when the installed template predates the committed hook.**
Compare the template the resolved `wl` would emit
(`wl init`-equivalent content, e.g. `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json`
hook content, or a `wl hooks print`-style helper) against the repo's committed
`.githooks/pre-push`; refuse (or warn with the exact remedy) when the committed
hook carries capability the template lacks.
- *Pros:* cheap and directly targeted at the silent-deletion mechanism; needs no
  version convention; naturally testable in the existing installer test with a
  stub `wl`; fail-loud, and can be made fail-soft-visible (`WARNING`) where a
  hard failure would be hostile.
- *Cons:* if implemented only in the installer it is an *install-time* guard —
  a later manual `wl doctor upgrade --confirm` bypasses it, so the durable
  "never downgrade a hook" guard belongs upstream in
  `ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` (with its own test) and this item
  should file that as a linked upstream item rather than assume it here.

### Recommendation

Implement **(c)** in the installer (fail-loud skew check, hermetic test,
documentation), because it is the smallest change that removes the silent
deletion path and it is testable in the existing installer suite. Follow it with
**(b)** as a cheap visibility convention (expected `worklog` version recorded
where the installer can read it), noting explicitly in the docs that the version
is a hint, not proof. Treat **(a)** as an **opt-in** flag
(`--refresh-wl`/`PI_REFRESH_WL=1`) rather than default behaviour, and file the
durable upstream guard (refuse a template "downgrade" inside `upgradeHooks`)
against `ContextHub` where the destructive write actually lives.

## Tests & documentation (explicitly in scope)

- This is a **shared framework script**, so the change cannot ship without
  tests: extend `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (existing, ~15 KB) with
  sandboxed-`HOME` cases — stale template + divergent committed hook
  (refusal/warning), up-to-date template (silent OK), `wl` absent (`wl`-not-found
  path must remain non-fatal, as the installer is fail-open elsewhere), and the
  opt-in refresh flag if (a) is taken.
- Documentation is part of the deliverable, not a follow-up: the installer's
  install notes, `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` (global install),
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (hook wiring) and the `README.md` install entry
  must describe the `wl` dependency and the remedy.
- Any "never downgrade" guard added in `ContextHub` needs its own test there
  (`../ContextHub/tests/`), as a separate `WL-` item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — hook-wiring block (:317-412); the place a skew check
  / opt-in refresh belongs.
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — the installer hook-wiring suite the
  new cases extend (sandboxed `HOME`).
- `../ContextHub/src/doctor/hook-upgrade.ts` — `PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT` and
  `upgradeHooks()` (:603-643, whole-file overwrite at :622) — the durable
  "never downgrade" guard target (separate `WL-` item).
- `../ContextHub/src/commands/doctor/upgrade.ts` — the `--dry-run` / `--confirm`
  CLI contract a dry-run-based skew check would consume.
- `../ContextHub/.gitignore` — line 86 (`dist`), the reason the template is not
  version-controlled.
- `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md` —
  documentation surface.

## Constraints

- The installer is shared across every framework project and must stay
  **fail-open** for non-hook concerns (it already warns rather than dies on a
  missing context-audit skill, missing thresholds, or a failed identity guard);
  only the hook-template skew guard may be fail-loud, and its exit behaviour
  needs an explicit decision (blocking vs `WARNING`) recorded in the item.
- No live-`HOME` mutations in tests: sandbox `HOME` (as the existing suite does).
- Do not rebuild a `ContextHub` checkout the operator did not ask to rebuild
  (option (a) must be opt-in), and never mutate another repository from a
  default install.
- Push to `dev` only, never `main`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the resolved `wl` on a framework host is the npm-linked
  `ContextHub` build (verified above); a registry install would make (a)
  meaningless but (c)/(b) still useful.
- **Risk:** a `wl` that cannot print its template (e.g. an older `wl` without a
  print path) forces the check to parse `wl doctor upgrade --dry-run --json` or
  to fall back to a version comparison — the fallback must be documented and
  must not turn into a hard failure on an old `wl`.
- **Risk:** failing the whole install on skew could block a machine whose only
  problem is a stale `dist`; prefer an actionable `WARNING` plus a clear remedy
  unless the producer prefers a hard failure.
- **Risk:** duplicate coverage with `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU`'s AC2 tail clause —
  that item explicitly records the gap and does **not** fix it, so this item is
  the fix, not a duplicate.

## Related work

- `CG-0MW1ZBKP0006U1YU` (Tableau-Card-Engine) — discovered-from; the
  template-ownership item whose AC2 tail clause records this gap.
- `WL-0MW20XXWE00466FP` (ContextHub) — the upstream template change
  (`mirror_suite_cache`), the capability whose silent removal motivated this.
- `SA-0MV8M4OVX000QHSM` (completed) — an earlier `install_pi.sh` hook-scope
  defect (v3 gate propagated to non-SorraAgents projects); same block, same
  fail-open principle.
- `SA-0MR3P8N3V001Q3RG` (completed) — "Add rebuild step to implement SKILL.md
  after git pull": the same stale-`dist` failure mode documented for agents,
  fixed by documentation rather than by an installer guard.
- `SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX` (completed) — the installer's git-identity guard, the
  precedent for "surface the problem at install time, fail-open".

## Deliverables

- `scripts/install_pi.sh` skew check (or opt-in refresh flag, per the recorded
  decision) with fail-loud/`WARNING` output naming both hook versions.
- New cases in `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` (sandboxed `HOME`).
- Documentation updates in the installer's install notes,
  `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md`, `docs/dev/context-budget.md`, `README.md`.
- A linked `WL-` item for the durable upstream "never downgrade" guard in
  `upgradeHooks()` (filed, not implemented here).

## Problem

`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py:_resolve_merge_base()` returns the **candidate ref name** (`origin/dev`) rather than the SHA resolved by `git merge-base`, and `compute_changed_files()` then runs `git diff --name-only <ref>` against that name.

When an implement worktree's branch base is *behind* the ref (a stale base — e.g. the branch was forked while local `dev` lagged `origin/dev`), diffing against the ref includes **dev-side** commits that are not part of the change set. `select_group_from_changed_files()` then picks test groups for unrelated work.

Discovered-from: WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ (ContextHub store) — the stale-base session in which this was observed.

## Evidence

- Observed on 2026-11-05 in a ContextHub implement session (WL-0MW3JIYIR002RCP8): a docs + `tests/setup-tests.ts` change set ran `npm test -- packages/herdr/src` because the stale base made the diff include dev-side `packages/herdr` commits.
- Current code (`run_tests.py`, `_resolve_merge_base`, ~line 506): the loop runs `git merge-base <candidate> HEAD`, then `return candidate` (the ref name) — the resolved `proc.stdout.strip()` SHA is discarded.
- `compute_changed_files()` (~line 462) passes the returned value straight into `git diff --name-only <base>`.

## Users

- **Implementation agents** running `implement.py finish` / `run_tests.py --scope changed` — depend on correct changed-file selection.
- **Operators / CI** — depend on changed-scope runs exercising the code that actually changed.

### Example user stories

- As an implementation agent, when my worktree forked from a base behind `origin/dev`, I want changed-scope selection to measure only *my* diff, so the gate runs the right tests.
- As an operator, I want a stale base to degrade into a smaller diff, never into an unrelated named group.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_resolve_merge_base()` returns the SHA resolved by `git merge-base` (falling back to the next candidate only when `merge-base` yields nothing), never a bare ref name.
- [ ] `compute_changed_files()` diffs against a merge-base SHA, so commits that exist on the ref but not on the branch base are excluded from the change set.
- [ ] Regression test: a fixture repo whose branch base is one commit behind the target ref — the changed-file set must contain only the branch's own files, not the ref-side files.
- [ ] Fallback behaviour preserved: with no usable base the function still returns `None` and callers fall back to full scope (no crash).
- [ ] Documentation updated where the changed-scope base semantics are described (`skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md`) if the returned value's contract changes.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Probe/read-only of git state; no new runtime dependencies; reuse existing helpers (`_git_inspection_env`, `run_cmd`).
- Behaviour change must be conservative: an unresolved base must still fall back to full scope rather than an empty diff.
- Related but distinct from SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66 (unqualified `origin/dev` ref *ambiguity* with a shadowing local branch) — both live in the same function, so either item may be implemented first; if both are taken together, keep the two fixes as separate commits.
- All written output in UK English.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `_resolve_merge_base()` must return the merge-base SHA; `compute_changed_files()` consumes it unchanged.
- `skill/test/tests/` (or the existing test-skill test location) — regression test for a stale-base fixture.
- `skill/test/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — document the returned-value contract if it is described there.

## Related work

- ContextHub `WL-0MW3LTY9A007ZULJ` — Main-checkout local dev diverged from origin/dev (the stale-base incident; records this hand-off).
- `SA-0MUH1P93R006NT66` — Stale local branch named origin/dev makes origin/dev ambiguous (adjacent defect in the same function).

# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)
- **WL-0MQZX8BTN006N4BF** – Automatically recover from appropriate server errors (completed)
- **WL-0MURJ0LFH002O95I** – r-i (Producer Interview) should focus on the created pane (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: access, back, category, click, completed, currently, defined, discovery, dry, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, information, key, layout, lets, list, load, one, output, paragraph, providing, readable, see, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: access, achieve, back, completed, currently, defined, describing, doing, end, etc, example, fit, focused, foo, group, ids, impact, improve, key, layout, list, load, one, output, paragraph, readable, see, setup, should, single, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: back, completed, defined, discovery, dry, easy, end, etc, fit, focused, foo, group, heavy, ids, improve, improved, key, list, load, one, output, readable, see, setup, should, single, speed, stability, standup, top, under, user, using, when, you

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-06: Plan decomposition complete (plan skill). 7 child work items created in test-first dependency order. AC coverage: 100%. Key Files validated.
  - WL-0MW5HUS5E001SG6H — Unit tests for Impact extraction
  - WL-0MW5HVPJP009MVPQ — Impact extraction implementation in generate_standup.py
  - WL-0MW5HVQ7Z006SI6Q — Impact-aware report rendering + TTS fallback
  - WL-0MW5HVQY30018XZR — Golden-output test for grouped no-ID report
  - WL-0MW5HVRPJ002OOCH — Update standup SKILL.md for agent-rendered clustered report
  - WL-0MW5HVSH9007RRNI — Add ## Impact completion convention to AGENTS.md
  - WL-0MW5HVT52002JASH — Documentation sweep and full test suite pass

## Problem

The audit runner's in-main-slot resume clears its own view of pending child screens but does not delete the on-disk signal file.

Observed on 2026-11-09 auditing `CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE` (Tableau-Card-Engine):

- Run 1 (12:09-12:11) emitted one in-main-slot child screen for `CG-0MW97UZ68001JTGK` and wrote `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE.pending-screens.json`.
- The child was then closed (duplicate, failure fixed upstream).
- Resume run (13:33-13:34) reported `"pending_child_screens": []` in its JSON and a `Ready to close: Yes` verdict, **but the signal file was still present afterwards**, still naming the closed child.

## Impact

`cmd_issue` bypasses the freshness gate while `pending-screens.json` names any child (SA-0MVSTZ71J001P67S). A stale file therefore forces every later audit of that item to re-run the whole Phase 1 pipeline (one model call each) even though nothing is pending — a silent, repeatable cost. The document says the signal 'is cleared automatically when no screens remain'; it is not.

## Reproduction

1. Audit an item with one unaudited child in default in-main-slot mode to get the pending signal written.
2. Persist/close the child so no screens remain, then re-run the parent audit.
3. Observe `pending_child_screens: []` in the JSON while `.worklog/audit-checkpoints/<id>.pending-screens.json` still lists the child.

## Expected

The signal file is removed (or rewritten empty and then removed) whenever the collected pending set is empty, on both the fresh-run and resume paths.

## Actual

The file persists with its previous content.

## Workaround applied

Deleted the stale file manually so the next audit can take the freshness fast path.

## Discovered from

CG-0MW917K7V009LMLE (Tableau-Card-Engine docs audit)
data.title: audit runner leaves stale pending-screens.json when no child screens remain

# Bug — a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files

discovered-from:SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40 (driving the parent AC4 test gap exposed it).

## Problem

`changed_scope_selection()` (`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`) resolves a
declared test **group** first and returns immediately:

```python
group_name = select_group_from_changed_files(changed, root)
if group_name is not None:
    group_cmds = group_commands(group_name, root)
    if group_cmds:
        return ChangedScopeSelection(list(group_cmds), ...)
```

When a change set touches **both** a path matched by a group (`paths`) and a
test file the group does not cover, the group's command replaces the file-level
selection instead of unioning with it. The edit-authored test file is then
silently absent from the changed-scope run.

### Observed (SA-0MVLKHY27005UK40)

Changed files:

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` → matches the `implement` group
  (`skill/implement/**`) → command `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings
  skill/implement/tests/`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py` (the file the run was verifying) → **dropped**

Result: `212 passed`, none of them the two newly added tests. Running with only
the test file changed selected it correctly (`212 passed` including the new
tests), so the loss is specific to the group short-circuit.

## Impact

A changed-scope run now executes every test file the change set touches — including an
edit-authored test outside a matched test group — so a green changed-scope run
actually includes the new tests instead of reporting success without running them.
(Before the fix a green run could pass while never executing the tests the author
just wrote; the dev-push full-suite gate was the only backstop.)

## Acceptance criteria

1. A selection where a group matches *and* other changed test files exist emits
   the group's commands **unioned** with the file-level selection (deduplicated,
   deterministic order), or fails closed to the full suite — never silently
   drops a changed test file.
2. A test pins the union (changed source under a group path + changed test file
   outside the group's directories); the emitted command lists both.
3. A test pins that a group-only match still emits exactly the group command
   (no behaviour change for the single-match case).
4. `run_tests.py --scope changed` on a change set containing
   `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` + `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
   selects `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.
5. Changed-scope tests pass; the dev-push full-suite gate is green.


## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `changed_scope_selection()` short-circuits
  on a matched group (the bug); `select_group_from_changed_files()` picks the
  group; `_commands_for_selected_tests()` builds the file-level commands and
  `group_commands()` resolves the group's declared commands.
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_scope.py` — changed-scope selection tests
  (`TestChangedScopeGroups`); the union + group-only regression tests (AC2/AC3)
  belong here.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_run_group_from_changed_files()` is
  a second, redundant group-first short-circuit: `_run_resolved_suite()` returns
  its result before `changed_scope_selection()` is consulted. See OPEN QUESTION.

## Test-first ordering

Write the failing union tests (AC2/AC3) first and confirm they reproduce the
drop against the current `changed_scope_selection()`, then fix. After the fix
the changed-scope run (AC4) must list `tests/test_implement_drive.py`.

## Suggested approach

1. In `changed_scope_selection()`, when a group matches, also resolve the
   file-level selection for changed test files **not** covered by the matched
   group's `paths`, then return the union: group commands first (declared
   order), then file-level commands (sorted), deduplicated. Keep the
   single-match (group-only) case byte-identical (AC3).
2. If the union cannot be constructed safely, fail closed to the full suite
   rather than dropping a changed test file (AC1).

## OPEN QUESTION

Is `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_run_group_from_changed_files()` in
scope for this item, or deferred to SA-0MVEJIHIG003WTH9 (changed-scope group
union + selector convergence, AC3)?

- Why it matters: fixing only `changed_scope_selection()` leaves the implement
  `finish` gate — the path this bug was observed through — still short-circuiting
  on the redundant group-first selector, so the same silent drop recurs there.
- Recommendation: converge the finish gate on `changed_scope_selection()` in the
  same change (it already honours groups, so the extra selector is dead
  duplication). Note that `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests_groups.py::
  test_implement_has_group_runner` asserts the function exists and must be
  updated if it is removed.
data.title: test skill: a matched changed-scope group silently drops other changed test files

discovered-from: SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV

## Goal

As an agent auditing a work item at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD, I want the audit's full-suite evidence check to reuse the tree-keyed verdict the dev-push gate just recorded for that same commit, so the first audit after every push does not pay for a second identical full-suite run.

## Problem statement

`SA-0MW7C6BMZ00931JG` (shipped `39ea226b4`) re-keyed the dev-push pre-push gate to the pushed commit's **tree** (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}`). The gate therefore no longer writes a loose-worktree-keyed entry for the pushed commit.

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_full_suite_cache_status` still queries the cache worktree-only (`query_cached(command, cwd=..., ttl=AUDIT_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS)`), following the documented contract in `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3 ("callers that pass nothing keep the historical worktree keys byte for byte (test-skill CLI, audit)").

Consequence, observed live during this epic's own audit at HEAD `ea89bb4e2`:

```
Automatic full-suite verification unavailable: 4 of 4 suite command(s) not verifiably green at HEAD ea89bb4e2 …
```

The gate had already gated that exact commit, yet the audit could not see the verdict and re-executed the whole suite (4 commands, several minutes). Before the tree keying, the gate's worktree-keyed run was mirrored into the main checkout cache and served the audit. This is the mirror image of the reuse gap `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` closed for finish → pre-push, now on the audit path.

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` already solved the identical problem for its own post-push verification (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`, `54d5b79f1`): resolve the pushed commit's tree, query `fingerprint_kind="tree"` first, then fall back to the loose worktree key. The audit path needs the same treatment.

## Desired change

- `_full_suite_cache_status` (and any sibling read-only evidence query that mirrors it, e.g. the `_phase_...` full-suite checks at `audit_runner.py:3559` and `:3767`) resolves the audited HEAD's tree (`git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) and queries the tree-kind entry **first**, falling back to the historical worktree query so legacy entries still count.
- A tree-kind entry accepted as evidence is reported with its `fingerprint_kind` and age, so a reused verdict is visible in the audit output rather than implied.
- `query_cached()`'s worktree-only default is unchanged for every other caller (the finish gate's staged-tree semantics depend on it).

## Acceptance criteria

1. An audit at a HEAD whose only cached full-suite evidence is tree-kind (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`, keyed on `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}`) reports full-suite evidence **without executing** the suite.
2. A worktree-kind (legacy) entry at the audited HEAD is still accepted, byte-for-byte keying unchanged.
3. An entry recorded for a *different* tree is a miss (a green verdict for another tree is never accepted).
4. The reused verdict's `fingerprint_kind` and age are reported in the audit output/JSON.
5. Deterministic tests cover: tree-kind hit (no execution), legacy worktree hit, different-tree miss, and the unchanged `query_cached()` default for other callers.
6. Documentation is updated: `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` §0.3/§0.4 and the audit-side note in `docs/dev/` describing the audit's evidence query, corrected from "worktree only" to "tree-kind first, worktree fallback".
7. Every new behaviour is exercised by an automated test executed through the test skill, and the full suite passes.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_full_suite_cache_status` and the sibling read-only cache queries.
- `skill/test_cache.py` — `query_cached(fingerprint=…, fingerprint_kind=…)` (already supports the tree kind; no new API expected).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — the `_resolve_post_push_verification` precedent (`SA-0MWAXC5TD00461FN`) to mirror.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — §0.3/§0.4 contract correction.
- `tests/` — new audit-evidence reuse tests (`tests/test_audit_full_suite_cache_tree.py` or the existing audit home).

## Impact

An agent auditing work at a freshly pushed `dev` HEAD reuses the gate's tree-keyed green verdict instead of re-running the same full suite, cutting the first audit after each push by roughly one full-suite execution.
data.title: Audit: reuse the tree-keyed dev-push gate verdict for full-suite evidence

## Shared helper: filing_location.py

### Goal
Pure, unit-testable, no-side-effects helper for detecting work-item filing location issues.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. The check deterministically classifies the item as one of ok, foreign, unregistered, absent, or suspicious. Each non-ok classification names the likely correct project (from the sibling scan) and a suggested target prefix.
2. The check lives in a new shared helper skill/shared/filing_location.py (pure, unit-testable, no side effects) invoked from the intake lifecycle script. No other skill changes behaviour in this change.
3. check_filing(item_id, *, cwd, sibling_scan_root, runner) returns FilingCheck with severity ok, foreign, unregistered, absent, or suspicious.
4. Uses existing resolve_worklog_dir, _extract_work_item_prefix, run_wl from status_lifecycle.py (no changes to those modules).
5. Sibling scan is memoized and respects SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT.
6. Content cross-check scans sibling repos' file trees respecting gitignore.
7. No network dependency - only reads config.yaml and runs wl show.
8. Injectable runner for testing.
9. Non-blocking and non-destructive by default - detection never fails intake nor mutates foreign stores; recreation requires explicit flag.
10. Idempotent - re-running the check on the same item yields the same result and never duplicates comments or recreations.

### Key Files
- skill/shared/filing_location.py (new)
- skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py - reuse resolve_worklog_dir, _extract_work_item_prefix, run_wl

## Intake CLI: check-filing subcommand and flags

### Goal
Add check-filing subcommand to intake.py and wire it as step 0c after claim. Add CLI flags for misfiled-item handling.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. skill:intake runs a filing-location check for the target work item before any other mutation, and reports its findings to the operator (stderr plus work-item comment). The check is non-blocking: intake proceeds whether or not the item passes the check.
2. On a non-ok classification the script logs a warning and records an idempotent filing location check comment on the item (re-runs update the existing comment, never duplicate). When stdin is an interactive TTY it additionally offers continue or recreate the item in the correct project. Auto-recreation is only possible via an explicit --misfiled-action recreate flag and never happens by default.
3. Recreating (when chosen) creates a new item under the target project's store/prefix copying title, description, tags, issue type and priority, records a Recreated from source-id reference, and closes the original with the reason Misfiled: recreated in target-project (target-id). A dry-run --dry-run mode prints the would-be recreation without creating.
4. intake.py gains a check-filing <id> subcommand that runs the filing check.
5. check-filing runs as step 0c right after claim in the intake flow.
6. CLI gains --misfiled-action {warn,offer,recreate} (default warn), --recreate-target <project-dir>, and --dry-run flags.
7. No other skill's behavior changes in this work item.
8. The check is non-blocking - intake proceeds whether or not the item passes.
9. Idempotent - re-running the check on the same item yields the same result and never duplicates comments or recreations.
10. Legitimate cross-project usage stays quiet - running intake from the SorraAgents checkout on a WL- item routed by prefix-to-sibling scan is supported behaviour.

### Key Files
- skill/intake/scripts/intake.py - check-filing subcommand + hookup
- skill/shared/filing_location.py - invoked by check-filing

# Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Test-first tracer bullet: write the regression tests **before** the fix. Expectations that
target the new behaviour carry `xfail(strict=True)` until the implementation child removes
the marker; expectations that already hold (the conservative failure paths, the
ancestry-not-equality rule) pass before and after, so a failing test can only be failing on
the behaviour under test.

## Goal

As an implementation agent, I want hermetic, deterministic tests that pin the remote-observed
push verdict, so a later change to `finish`'s push-outcome handling can never silently regress
into reporting a landed push as a failure — nor into claiming success for a commit that never
reached `origin/dev`.

## Context

`finish` treats the exit status of `git push` as the sole verdict on whether the commit reached
`origin/dev`, so a push interrupted after the remote accepted the ref (timeout, process-group
kill, late non-zero exit) is reported as a failure and the item is reset to `open`. The only
remote check today is the post-*success* ancestry assertion
(`_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()`, `implement.py` L8084), which runs after a push already
claimed success — nothing distinguishes "landed but interrupted" from "never landed". No
existing test simulates the race: `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py`,
`tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` and
`skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` all assume the push verdict is truthful.

## Scope

Tests only — no production-code change in this slice. Deliver the failing baselines that the
implementation child turns green, plus the companion tests that prove the preconditions (a
real hermetic push, a reachable bare remote, a real terminal read-back) rather than assuming
them.

## Key Files

- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — new hermetic suite: probe variants, the three outcomes, sibling-push ancestry.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — existing interrupted-push coverage; extend where a case belongs there.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push baseline (a retry that lands but is reported as failed).
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — reusable `init_bare_remote` / `init_repo` / `add_worktree` / `commit_all` factories; reuse rather than hand-rolling fixtures.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the `FakeGitBoundary` stubbed-boundary harness style for end-to-end `phase_finish` tests.

## Constraints

- **Hermetic:** self-contained bare remote plus clone/worktree under `tmp_path`; never mutate the live checkout's refs, never touch the shared `refs/heads/dev`, no network access.
- **Unambiguous baselines:** pair each new-behaviour `xfail(strict=True)` with a companion that passes before and after, so the preconditions are proven separately instead of being smuggled into the baseline.
- **No hiding failures:** `xfail(strict=True)` only where the expectation targets the not-yet-implemented behaviour.
- **Test execution policy:** no agent-initiated `pytest`/`run_tests.py` invocation outside `/skill:test` (`implement.py finish`'s changed-scope gate and the dev-push gate are infrastructure and out of scope).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Interrupted push variants are covered by unit tests.** Unit tests drive each interrupted-push variant — `PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, and a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward — and assert the remote verification probe runs before any push failure is reported: it verifies whether the commit being pushed is reachable from the remote `dev` tip (`git ls-remote origin refs/heads/dev` plus a fetch of that ref and `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>`), is time-bounded, uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite), and applies to the non-fast-forward retry push as well as the first push.
- **Verified-landed success end-to-end.** An end-to-end hermetic test against a bare remote plus a clone under `tmp_path` — where the remote already contains the commit and the push hangs past a short timeout — asserts `report["success"] is True`, the push step is marked `verified_after_failure`, the completion comment naming the commit is posted, the existing success-path cleanup runs (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), and the work item is `completed`/`in_review` with the terminal read-back still passing.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome are distinguished.** Negative tests — a remote without the commit, and a verification probe that itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error) — assert `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Hermetic regression coverage, ancestry not equality.** The new tests are hermetic (self-contained bare remote plus clone under `tmp_path`; no live checkout or live `refs/heads/dev` mutation, no network access) and cover an interrupted push that landed, an interrupted push that did not land, a verification probe failure, and a sibling push advancing `origin/dev` after ours (ancestry, not equality, must be accepted); they fail without the fix (or exercise the new helper directly) and pass with it, reusing the `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` factories.
data.title: Hermetic interrupted-push verdict tests
